In my country, education is a subject which every family talks about. It is important to note that not only the government but also the parents have a responsibility here. When I was a student in secondary school, my teacher told us that the exam is the only door to a good life, and many of my friends believed this. They studied fifteen hours in a day and they forgot to sleep.

However, I think that this way of thinking creates a big problem for young people. A student who only memorises will not develop the skill of thinking by himself. Moreover, the pressure makes many students to lose the motivation completely. In my class, three students left the school before the final year, and all of them were clever.

For this reason I believe that the education system must change. The schools should teach not only the knowledge but also how to use it in the real life. Furthermore, the families should understand that a child is not a machine. Additionally, the teachers need a better training, because a teacher who is tired cannot help anybody.

In conclusion, education plays a crucial role in the future of my country, and we must repair it before another generation is lost.

We stayed at this hotel for four nights in late September, which is generally the best time to visit this part of the coast, and I want to give a fair account rather than a list of complaints.

The location is genuinely good. It typically takes eight or nine minutes to walk to the old harbour, and the road, although narrow, is lit at night. The room itself was clean and larger than the photographs suggest. The air conditioning could be noisy, and it may bother a light sleeper, but it worked.

The breakfast is where opinions will differ. It is worth noting that the buffet is small by the standards of the big resorts, and it does not change much from day to day. That said, the bread was baked on site and the eggs were cooked to order, which for me counts for more than twelve kinds of packaged cake.

The staff were the reason we would return. Two of them remembered our names by the second morning, and when our taxi failed to arrive the manager drove us to the bus station himself.

Overall, this is a solid, unpretentious place that knows what it is and does not pretend otherwise. It might not suit somebody who wants a spa and four restaurants, but for a couple who want to walk into town and sleep, it is hard to beat at the price.

I have been coming to this village for eleven years, long before anybody wrote about it, and I still think it is the best decision I ever made with a fortnight of annual leave.

The guesthouse is nestled in the heart of the old quarter, up a lane too narrow for cars, which means you carry your own bag for the last two hundred metres. That filter is the whole point. Whether you are travelling alone or dragging two teenagers who would rather be at a water park, the lane sorts out what kind of holiday you are about to have.

Breakfast is at eight because that is when Nadia makes it, not because a sign says so. If you are late, you get bread and jam and a shrug, which is fair.

I am not going to pretend the plumbing is modern. The shower runs hot for four minutes and then makes a decision of its own. But I have slept better in that back room, with the shutters open and the church bell every hour, than in any hotel I have been sent to for work.

Nowadays, many people discuss whether the university education must be free for everybody. In my opinion, this question is not simple and it has two sides which we should look carefully.

First, a free university system gives the chance to the poor families. In my hometown, many clever students could not continue because their family cannot pay. Second, when the education is free, the country gets more engineers and doctors, and this plays a vital role in the development of the economy. Third, the student who does not think about the money can focus on the study.

However, there is another side. Free education is expensive for the government and the money comes from the taxes. Furthermore, when everybody goes to the university, the value of the diploma becomes less. Moreover, some students enter the university only because it is free, and they leave after one year.

Finally, I believe the best solution is a middle way. The state should pay for the students who are successful and who need the help, and the others should pay a small amount. In conclusion, education is not only a personal investment but also a national one, and the policy must reflect both.
